key_insight: Whole-genome sequencing in Latin American patients with early-onset or familial Parkinson’s identified several pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants that standard array-based screening could miss.
clinical_relevance: Genetic screening may improve the detection of monogenic Parkinson’s risk in underrepresented Latin American populations and help clarify early-onset or familial cases.
method: Short-read whole-genome sequencing was performed in 263 participants with early-onset and/or familial Parkinson’s disease.
The cohort had no previously known pathogenic Parkinson’s variant on genotyping data.
Researchers screened 7 Parkinson’s-related genes plus 21 genes linked to related parkinsonian disorders.
evidence_signal: In this sequenced subset, 4.7% had pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in primary or secondary Parkinson’s genes, 5.5% had pathogenic or likely pathogenic Gaucher disease variants, and 2.7% carried known GBA1 risk variants.
watch_item: Because the analysis focused on a selected subgroup without prior known pathogenic variants, findings may not generalize to all Parkinson’s patients and still require careful variant interpretation.
paper_title: Genomic Landscape of Early-Onset and Familial Latin American Parkinson's Patients
